neighbors.title: Citation-Enforced RAG for Fiscal Document Intelligence: Cited, Explainable Knowledge Retrieval in Tax Compliance
Citation Grounding: Detecting and Reducing LLM Citation Hallucinations via Legal Citation Graphs

related_work_framing.overlap: Citation-enforced domain RAG, citation-grounding metrics, and compact QA memories overlap with the project's citation and amortization story.
related_work_framing.distinction: The project must claim only update-heldout model/scaffold-side amortization from expensive grounded behavior, with citation existence, support/relevance, temporal validity, abstention support, coverage, and cost reported together.

dimensions.question: Can cited source ids be made syntactically/existentially valid?

rows.evidence: Deterministic citation repair reaches perfect inline citation syntax on the local Qwen 3B control.
Tiny SFT preserves citation format but not support.
longcite-style-citation-sft-comparison-2026-06-26-v1 shows citation-SFT framing is necessary but insufficient.

dimensions.question: Are claims supported by the cited evidence, not just cited?

rows.evidence: Direct compact-RAG answers have meaningful but incomplete answer support.
The current support-first guard improves support by losing coverage.
Syntax repair changes citation formatting but provides no judged support evidence.

dimensions.question: Does the system respect dated/update-heldout KB state?

rows.evidence: A naive cited-answer baseline fails stale-snapshot abstentions despite inline citation syntax.
A simple snapshot-aware retriever solves the deterministic stale-snapshot diagnostic but is not a trained student.
Legal citation grounding makes temporal validity a first-class citation metric; this project must report analogous update validity instead of syntax alone.

dimensions.question: Could the same economics be explained by compact memory or write-back instead of a distilled model/scaffold?

rows.evidence: Train-only write-back cannot answer eval updates on the versioned diagnostic.
Live snapshot retrieval plus train write-back can solve the toy diagnostic, so memory-side amortization remains a real baseline family.
FD-RAG-style compact QA memories are a close memory-side amortization neighbor that needs comparison or explicit scoping.

dimensions.question: What is the paper target if citation grounding and compact memory already exist?

rows.evidence: The target remains unproven until trained Qwen 3B predictions and paid grounded judging exist.
faithful-context-qa-comparison-2026-06-27-v1 scopes compact faithful-context QA as a close final-system baseline.
writeback-kb-amortization-scoped-exclusion-2026-06-26-v1 scopes memory-side write-back as a competing amortization route, not the current claim.

synthesis.headline: Citation grounding and compact memory are close enough that the paper must separate citation syntax, citation support, temporal validity, and amortization target.
claim_boundary: Do not claim citation-enforced domain RAG as new.
Do not claim citation grounding or citation-hallucination detection as new.
Do not claim compact-memory or federated RAG amortization as the contribution.
Claim model/scaffold-side amortization only after the trained Qwen 3B row passes support, coverage, temporal/update, and cost gates.
true_baseline_or_scope_needed: Report citation existence, citation support/relevance, and temporal/update validity separately.
Compare against a compact-memory/write-back baseline on the final update-heldout window, or explicitly scope it as memory-side amortization with leakage risks.
For any legal/fiscal citation-grounding comparison, explain domain-graph availability differences instead of implying direct comparability.
After Qwen 3B smoke, add the trained row to this comparison and the distillation-loss accounting table.

llm_budget.note: This comparison reads existing local artifacts and primary-source metadata already captured in the novelty watchlist.
